![](/home/jake/Developer/Course_Academy/reference/mathacademy/capture/multivariable/14222582/assets/b0e8cbe1a26b5a012f6098b67320070e882fa38783d8eda07dd0b76011a47b21.png)

The region enclosed by the curves $x=\frac{1}{y}$ and $x=\frac{5}{2}-y$ is rotated ${360}^{∘}$ about the line $x=-1.$ Which of the following gives the volume of the resulting solid?
question.worked_solution:
First, we want to determine the limits of integration. We find the intersections of the curves by solving the following equation:

$$
\begin{aligned}\frac{1}{y} & =\frac{5}{2}-y \\ 1 & =\frac{5}{2}y-{y}^{2} \\ {y}^{2}-\frac{5}{2}y+1 & =0 \\ 2{y}^{2}-5y+2 & =0 \\ (y-2)(2y-1) & =0 \\ y & =\frac{1}{2},2\end{aligned}
$$

Hence, our limits of integration are from $y=\frac{1}{2}$ to $y=2.$

Now, let's draw a horizontal arrow through the given region. The arrow should be pointing away from the axis of rotation.

![](/home/jake/Developer/Course_Academy/reference/mathacademy/capture/multivariable/14222582/assets/d5067706f9ff1abbdfd9dfce94711cb854f79c1156ddc0d81c1c35a5ed555f7a.png)

The horizontal arrow 

- *enters* the region through the inner curve $x=\frac{1}{y},$ and

- *leaves* through the outer curve $x=\frac{5}{2}-y.$

Next, we can find the volume of our solid as the difference between the volumes of the solids generated by the outer and inner curves.

- **Step I.** Figure out the volume generated by the outer curve $x=\frac{5}{2}-y.$

![](/home/jake/Developer/Course_Academy/reference/mathacademy/capture/multivariable/14222582/assets/a944979bc352b0e40afea73836b22c1fb1513fabbc727fb60d4c96793ee6fbb5.png)

The corresponding volume is given by

$$
\begin{aligned}{V}_{\text{outer}} & =\pi {\int }_{1/2}^{2}[\,(\text{right})-(\text{left})\,]^{2}\,\text{d}y \\  & =\pi {\int }_{1/2}^{2}{[\,(\frac{5}{2}-y)-(-1)\,]}^{2}\,\text{d}y \\  & =\pi {\int }_{1/2}^{2}{[\frac{7}{2}-y]}^{2}\,\text{d}y.\end{aligned}
$$

- **Step II.** Figure out the volume generated by the inner curve $x=\frac{1}{y}.$

![](/home/jake/Developer/Course_Academy/reference/mathacademy/capture/multivariable/14222582/assets/1eb04cf2f3ae0669dd82106b064dd822da618e9ca31bb3b96e4e30c71b7c3193.png)

The corresponding volume is given by

$$
\begin{aligned}{V}_{\text{inner}} & =\pi {\int }_{1/2}^{2}[\,(\text{right})-(\text{left})\,]^{2}\,\text{d}y \\  & =\pi {\int }_{1/2}^{2}{[\,(\frac{1}{y})-(-1)\,]}^{2}\,\text{d}y \\  & =\pi {\int }_{1/2}^{2}{[\frac{1}{y}+1]}^{2}\,\text{d}y.\end{aligned}
$$

- **Step III.** Find the difference.

Finally, we can write the volume of the original solid as

$$
\begin{aligned}V & ={V}_{\text{outer}}-{V}_{\text{inner}} \\  & =\pi {\int }_{1/2}^{2}{[\frac{7}{2}-y]}^{2}\,\text{d}y-\pi {\int }_{1/2}^{2}{[\frac{1}{y}+1]}^{2}\,\text{d}y \\  & =\pi {\int }_{1/2}^{2}({[\frac{7}{2}-y]}^{2}-{[\frac{1}{y}+1]}^{2})\text{d}y.\end{aligned}
$$
